claim.quote: In 1965, the first cosmic ray neutrino was observed in KGF by the Tata-Osaka-Durham group (Ref.3).

date.note: Year precision. The quote gives the year of the observation; the discovery paper is Phys. Lett. 18, 196 (August 1965) according to Crossref metadata (page not fetchable), whose DOI is recorded under publication.
date.quote: in early 1965 they recorded the first atmospheric-neutrino event

name: Detection of muons produced by cosmic ray neutrinos deep underground
notes: Priority is shared: the CERN Courier obituary says the Kolar event was recorded 'contemporaneously with the detection from another underground neutrino experiment set up by Fred Reines in a South African mine'.
The primary 1965 paper could not be fetched, so the claim quote is the collaboration's own 2000 statement.

summary.plain: In early 1965 neutrino telescopes 2.3 kilometres down in the Kolar Gold Fields mine recorded the first neutrino made by cosmic rays in the atmosphere. A South African mine experiment saw its own first atmospheric neutrino at about the same time.
summary.technical: Seven neutrino telescopes at 2300 m depth recorded muons from atmospheric-neutrino interactions in early 1965, contemporaneously with Reines' South African mine experiment; the rate agreed with the calculated flux from pion, kaon and muon decays.

title: Detection of muons produced by cosmic ray neutrinos deep underground
why_it_matters: The first observation of neutrinos from cosmic rays, which opened underground neutrino physics.
